text: dsh-phone 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的电话与消息侧栏插件，通过 web 面板、服务器路由和 agent 工具连接电话线路与 Telegram。用户可以在侧栏查看和发送短信、拨打或接听电话、管理来电模式、查看语音信箱及转写，并使用 Telegram 聊天功能。插件也注册电话状态、短信和诊断等 agent 工具；电话线路可配置 Twilio 或 SIP。使用 Twilio 需要相应账户和凭据；Mistral 转写为可选服务，音频会发送到其转写接口。

dsh-phone adds phone, SMS, voicemail, and Telegram features to the DSH web sidebar. It registers agent tools for phone status, messaging, and diagnostics, and supports Twilio or SIP lines. Optional Mistral transcription sends voicemail audio to its service.
想在 DSH 网页里收发短信和接听电话。
需要从 DSH 侧栏管理来电、语音信箱和电话线路。
Can I handle Telegram chats and phone calls from my DSH web interface?
dsh-phone 的功能「短信与电话」：在 DSH 网页侧栏查看短信会话、发送短信以及拨打和接听电话；也可选择来电处理模式。短信发送可由 agent 工具生成草稿或执行发送。
dsh-phone 的功能「语音信箱转写」：来电可进入语音信箱，插件支持查看留言及转写文本；转写可配置本地端点或 Mistral 服务，也可关闭。
dsh-phone 使用 Twilio 线路时，电话和短信功能会与 Twilio 服务交互；配置 Twilio 账户凭据后才能使用对应线路（见 daemon/twilio.mjs:101、lib/index.js:86-93）。
dsh-phone 选择 Mistral 转写时会将语音留言音频发送到 api.mistral.ai；此服务为可选项，也可配置本地转写端点（见 daemon/transcribe.mjs:65-75）。

SMS, calls, live voicemail and Telegram in the DSH sidebar, with call audio through your own server.

Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone`, or from GitHub: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-phone`.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-better-sidebar   # the tab host, skip if installed
dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · restart dsh web, then run phone-hookd and connect your provider (see Install)：- **Text**: SMS threads, send and receive, delivery status, MMS pictures, segment counter (GSM-7 / Unicode).
- **Call**: place and answer calls in the browser, mute, keypad (DTMF), call log. **Call audio goes through your server by default** ("Via server": one encrypted wss socket to the DSH origin, so it works on networks that block WebRTC and the browser talks to no third party); **Direct** (WebRTC to Twilio through the Twilio Voice SDK) stays one click away. A **Test audio** button checks a network without placing a call.
- **Choose how calls reach you**, with one switch:
  - **Live**: calls ring this browser (and optionally a mobile, which must press 1 so its own voicemail cannot steal the call). Unanswered calls go to voicemail.
  - **Voicemail**: every call goes to voicemail. While the caller speaks you see a **live transcript** and can **Pick up** (hot answer), like iOS Live Voicemail.
  - **Do not disturb**: calls go to voicemail and nothing rings, chimes or notifies. Starred contacts can still ring. Optional auto reply by SMS.

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · restart dsh web, then run phone-hookd and connect your provider (see Install)：dsh-phone is provider-agnostic by design. **Twilio is the first adapter** (done, tested on a real line). Next: any **SIP account or trunk** through a relay on your server (for example an existing landline from a local VoIP provider), Twilio-compatible **SignalWire**, then Telnyx, Vonage, Plivo and SMS gateways. A SIP account (an existing landline) can join through an Asterisk relay in bridge mode: **[docs/RELAY.md](docs/RELAY.md)**. See **[docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md)** for every option, the standards behind each setting (SIP, WebRTC, SRTP, codecs, DTMF, E.164, SMS encodings) and which setup to pick.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · How it fits together：- **phone-hookd** (`daemon/hookd.mjs`) is a small Node service that owns the database and talks to the provider. It has two listeners:
  - a **public** one (`127.0.0.1:3098`, exposed only as `https://<host>/phone-hook/`) for provider webhooks. Every request must carry a valid `X-Twilio-Signature`; anything else gets 403.
  - a **private** unix socket (`~/.dsh/phone/hookd.sock`, mode 0600) used only by the plugin.
  It runs outside the web UI on purpose: calls still reach voicemail and texts still arrive while the UI restarts.
- **The plugin** (`lib/index.js`) runs inside dsh-web. It registers the settings, the agent tools and `/dsh-phone/api/*`, where every request passes the same four gates as dsh-mail / dsh-hpc (loopback peer, same-origin trust fence, short-lived capability token, harness session cookie) before it is forwarded to the socket. It also serves the Voice SDK locally (no CDN).
- **The browser half** (`src/client.jsx`, built to `lib/client.js`) starts one phone service per page: live events (SSE), the Twilio Device, a WebAudio ringtone, browser notifications, and an overlay for incoming calls, the active call, live vo

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Call audio: Via server (default) or Direct：With **Via server** the browser captures the microphone (echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain on), encodes G.711 mu-law in an AudioWorklet and sends 20 ms blocks over ONE wss socket to the DSH origin (`/dsh-phone/api/io`, about 70 kbit/s each way at the default 40 ms per message); far audio plays through a small adaptive jitter buffer. No Twilio SDK, CDN, STUN or TURN is loaded. phone-hookd bridges the socket to the call:
section: Call audio: Via server (default) or Direct

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Call audio: Via server (default) or Direct：- **SIP lines** (an Asterisk relay): hookd originates an AudioSocket channel over AMI into a generated context that applies the line's destination policy and dials the provider. Audio between Asterisk and hookd stays on 127.0.0.1. Twilio is not involved.
- **Twilio lines** and **every incoming call you answer here**: a bidirectional Twilio Media Stream (`<Connect><Stream>`, mu-law 8 kHz) to `wss://<host>/phone-hook/s`, accepted only with a valid `X-Twilio-Signature` over the wss URL and a one-time ticket bound to the CallSid. Incoming calls ring the Phone tab through the event stream while the caller hears ringback from the server; unanswered or declined calls go to voicemail as before, and **Pick up** on a live voicemail works the same way.
- Per-call audio stats (route, packets and bytes each way, jitter, first-audio time, end reason) are stored with the call log row, so a silent call can be diagnosed from the server. Nothing is recorded beyond the voicemail you already have.
- Limits: `audio.maxCalls` (default 2) calls and `audio.maxTests` (2) tests at once; a dropped browser socket keeps the call for 15

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Settings (namespace `dsh-phone`)：The incoming-call **mode** itself is runtime state (the switch in the tab, or `phone_set_mode`), so flipping it never rewrites your settings file. `incoming.defaultMode` only applies to a fresh database.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Costs (Twilio, late 2026)：Calls on the server route over a Twilio line are billed as a normal PSTN call plus Media Streams (0.0044 USD per minute); SIP-line calls on the server route do not touch Twilio at all. Direct browser calls are billed as Twilio Client minutes plus the PSTN leg; SMS per segment (Greek lowercase is Unicode: 70 characters per segment); the live voicemail transcript uses Twilio real-time transcription (about 0.027 USD per minute, voicemail only); the final transcript is local and free; recordings are deleted from Twilio after download, so there is no storage charge.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Telegram：A Telegram account on the server, in its own Phone tab section: chats, groups and channels, photos, voice messages (transcribed by the voicemail engine) and files, channel posts, 1:1 voice calls on the server audio route, and `telegram_*` agent tools, with the browser talking only to the DSH origin. A Go daemon (`telegramd/`, MTProto via gotd/td) holds the account behind a private unix socket.

Setup in short (details in [docs/TELEGRAM.md](docs/TELEGRAM.md)):

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Telegram：Terms caveat: Telegram watches accounts that log in through third-party API clients, and flooding or spam gets an account banned. The agent tools therefore only write to existing conversations or allowlisted chats, with rate limits, an audit log and a kill switch; read "Rules for automated use" in docs/TELEGRAM.md before you enable agent sending. Use it on your own account at your own risk.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Telegram：Voice calls use [ntgcalls](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls) (`libntgcalls`, LGPL-3.0). It is **not** part of this repository: `telegramd/scripts/fetch-ntgcalls.sh` downloads the pinned release (v3.0.5) and checks its sha256, and `go build -tags ntgcalls` (cgo) links it dynamically, so you can replace the library with your own build. Without the build tag, telegramd builds as pure Go and calls report that the engine is missing; chats, media and transcription work either way.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Security：See [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md). In short: the only unauthenticated path is the signature-checked webhook prefix, served by a hardened daemon that never reaches the web UI; secrets are never returned by any read endpoint; sending and calling from agents are opt-in and draft-first.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · Development：```bash
npm test            # signature (Twilio's published vector), JWT, TwiML, E.164, segments, settings, store
npm run build       # src/client.jsx -> lib/client.js (verified before it replaces the live file)
```

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · When something goes wrong：- Ask your agent to load the **`phone-doctor`** skill (bundled in `skills/phone-doctor/`). The plugin registers it with the skills service at start, so it is offered after `dsh web` restarts. If your DSH does not list it, copy it once by hand: `P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-phone/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))"); mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/phone-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"` (see [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here)).
- One-call self-check: `GET /dsh-phone/api/doctor` (same access rules as the other read routes) or the read-only agent tool `phone_doctor`. It reports settings mode, lines, provider credentials (set or missing, never the values), the public webhook URL (set or not), whether the hook daemon answers on its private socket, SIP account registrations and the media server configuration. It never calls the provider, never places a call or sends a text, and failing checks carry a `PHONE_*` code and a hint. The read-only commands in [section 0 of the trou

@lucagiftzek/dsh-phone README · When something goes wrong：MIT licence. The Twilio Voice SDK is Apache-2.0 and is served from `node_modules`, not committed. libntgcalls (optional, Telegram calls) is LGPL-3.0, fetched by a script and linked dynamically, never committed.
